A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the isobars and pion crossed-box processes are essential ingredients for an accurate description of the NN interaction in the pseudophysical regime.
a chiral model for πN scattering, which is in accord with the πN phase shifts, leads to a nucleon-nucleus potential that is consistent with the empirical nucleon-nuclei phase shifts.
we have shown the importance of the Δ(1232) and ρ-meson in the NN interaction, and the need for explicit pion crossed-box terms in the chiral model of the NN interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NN interaction is not a simple sum of one-boson exchange potentials.
the NN interaction can be understood in a consistent way in terms of a chiral model of pion-nucleon scattering.
a realistic model of the NN interaction must include explicit pion crossed-box processes, and that a short-range repulsive interaction can be generated dynamically from isobar contributions.
